q-183348.name: Question 1
q-183348.problem:
$\,$ If $x$ has more than three divisors, then $x$ is composite.

Which of the following is logically equivalent to the conditional predicate above?
q-183348.worked_solution:
Let's denote by $P(x)$ and $Q(x)$ the following predicates:

- $P(x):$ $x$ has more than three divisors.

- $Q(x):$ $x$ is composite.

Then, our initial sentence can be written as $P(x)⇒Q(x),$ which is logically equivalent to 

$$
¬P(x)∨Q(x).
$$

The negation of $P(x)$ can be written as

- $¬P(x):$ $x$ doesn't have more than three divisors.

Therefore, the given sentence is logically equivalent to the following:

$\,$ $x$ doesn't have more than three divisors, or $x$ is composite.

Question 1
?

If x has more than three divisors, then x is composite.

Which of the following is logically equivalent to the conditional predicate above?

a
x doesn't have more than three divisors, and x is composite.
b
x has more than three divisors, or x is composite.
c
x has more than three divisors, and x is composite.
d
x doesn't have more than three divisors, or x is not composite.
e
x doesn't have more than three divisors, or x is composite.
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let's denote by P(x) and Q(x) the following predicates:

  • P(x): x has more than three divisors.

  • Q(x): x is composite.

Then, our initial sentence can be written as P(x)⇒Q(x), which is logically equivalent to

¬P(x)∨Q(x).

The negation of P(x) can be written as

  • ¬P(x): x doesn't have more than three divisors.

Therefore, the given sentence is logically equivalent to the following:

x doesn't have more than three divisors, or x is composite.

q-183355.name: Question 2
q-183355.problem:
Consider the following predicates.

$\,$ $A(x):$ $x\in Z.$ $\,$ $B(x):$ $-x\in Z.$

Which of the following is equivalent to the biconditional predicate $A(x)⇔B(x)?$

I. If $x\in Z$ then $-x\in Z$, and if $-x\in Z$ then $x\in Z.$

II. $x\in Z$ is equivalent to $-x\in Z.$

III. $x\in Z$ if and only if $-x\in Z.$
q-183355.worked_solution:
A biconditional expression $P⇔Q≡(P⇒Q)∧(Q⇒P)$ can be read as shown below:

- $P$ if and only if $Q$

- $P$ is equivalent to $Q$

- If $P$ then $Q,$ and if $Q$ then $P$

So, $A⇔B$ translates into the following sentences:

- $x\in Z$ if and only if $-x\in Z.$

- $x\in Z$ is equivalent to $-x\in Z.$

- If $x\in Z$ then $-x\in Z$, and if $-x\in Z$ then $x\in Z.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I, II, and III."

- $P$ if and only if $Q$

- $P$ is equivalent to $Q$

- If $P$ then $Q,$ and if $Q$ then $P$

q-183375.name: Question 4
q-183375.problem:
For the universal set $U,$ given by

$$
U=\{2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9\},
$$

find the truth set of $P(x)⇔Q(x)$ for the following predicates: 

- $P(x):$ $x$ is prime.

- $Q(x):$ $3\,|\,x.$
q-183375.worked_solution:
Since we have that

$$
P(x)⇔Q(x)≡(P(x)∧Q(x))∨(¬P(x)∧¬Q(x)),
$$

the corresponding truth set can be found as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}_{P⇔Q}=({T}_{P}\cap {T}_{Q})\cup ({\overset{―}{T}}_{P}\cap {\overset{―}{T}}_{Q})\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that:

- The truth set of $P(x)$ is 

$$
{T}_{P}=\{2,3,5,7\}
$$

and its complement is

$$
{\overset{―}{T}}_{P}=\{4,6,8,9\}.
$$

- The truth set of $Q(x)$ is 

$$
{T}_{Q}=\{3,6,9\}
$$

 
and its complement is

$$
{\overset{―}{T}}_{Q}=\{2,4,5,7,8\}.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}_{P}\cap {T}_{Q} & =\{2,3,5,7\}\cap \{3,6,9\} \\  & =\{3\} \\ {\overset{―}{T}}_{P}\cap {\overset{―}{T}}_{Q} & =\{4,6,8,9\}\cap \{2,4,5,7,8\} \\  & =\{4,8\} \\ {T}_{P⇔Q} & =({T}_{P}\cap {T}_{Q})\cup ({\overset{―}{T}}_{P}\cap {\overset{―}{T}}_{Q}) \\  & =\{3\}\cup \{4,8\} \\  & =\{3,4,8\}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4
?

For the universal set U, given by

U={2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9},

find the truth set of P(x)⇔Q(x) for the following predicates:

  • P(x): x is prime.

  • Q(x): 3|x.

a
{3,4,8}
b
{3,6,9}
c
{2,4,5,7,8}
d
{4,6,8,9}
e
{4,8}
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Since we have that

P(x)⇔Q(x)≡(P(x)∧Q(x))∨(¬P(x)∧¬Q(x)), the corresponding truth set can be found as follows:

TP⇔Q=(TP∩TQ)∪(T―P∩T―Q)

Notice that:

  • The truth set of P(x) is TP={2,3,5,7} and its complement is T―P={4,6,8,9}.

  • The truth set of Q(x) is TQ={3,6,9} and its complement is T―Q={2,4,5,7,8}.

Therefore, we have

TP∩TQ={2,3,5,7}∩{3,6,9}={3}T―P∩T―Q={4,6,8,9}∩{2,4,5,7,8}={4,8}TP⇔Q=(TP∩TQ)∪(T―P∩T―Q)={3}∪{4,8}={3,4,8}.
